questions.q: Where has Jarvis gone while the survey sticks stand untouched in the valley?
choices: To Pretoria — his business is 'surely the business of the sticks, which was the business of the dam'
questions.explain: Kumalo waits more and more for news of Jarvis's return.

questions.q: Whom does Kumalo increasingly believe can 'perform the great miracle' for Ndotsheni?
questions.explain: Kuluse's child has recovered on the milk Jarvis sent.

questions.q: What does the small white boy come to the church to do?
choices: 'Talk Zulu again' — Kumalo teaches him words like amanzi (water), ihashi (horse), inkomo (cow)
questions.explain: By the end he can say a whole sentence, and Kumalo claps his hands in delight.

questions.q: What Zulu sentence does Kumalo say to the boy, meaning 'when you are gone, something bright will go out of Ndotsheni'?
choices: A tribute to the boy — the child laughs with pleasure and makes Kumalo repeat it
questions.explain: The boy has 'a brightness inside him', like his father Arthur before him.

questions.q: Who arrives to stay at the church, sent by Jarvis?
choices: Napoleon Letsitsi, a young agricultural demonstrator, 'come here to teach farming'
questions.explain: Kumalo, overjoyed, tells him 'You are an angel from God.'

questions.q: How did Jarvis come to hire Letsitsi?
choices: Jarvis went to his home in Krugersdorp, where he was teaching, and asked if he would do 'a great work' at Ndotsheni — for ten pounds a month
questions.explain: Xosa and Zulu are 'almost the same', and Letsitsi's mother was a Xosa.

questions.q: What does Letsitsi say he would do in a valley like Ndotsheni?
choices: Stop the burning of dung and put it back in the land, gather and treat the weeds, plough round the hills, plant quick-growing trees for fuel, and share the land for pastures
Move the people to the towns
questions.explain: Hardest of all, he says, is the custom of lobola, which makes people keep too many cattle.

questions.q: Where is the water for the planned dam to come from?
choices: By a pipe from the river — 'That will be his [Jarvis's] river,' says Kumalo
questions.explain: Water from the dam can be let out to irrigate the land and the pastures.

questions.q: Why does the small white boy gallop back a second time — 'That was a close shave', he says?
choices: His grandfather came back early enough that he still had time to ride down and say goodbye — he leaves for Johannesburg on the small train tomorrow
questions.explain: 'Close shave' is slang, he explains — 'a narrow escape.'

questions.q: What does Letsitsi say about how quickly the valley can be restored?
choices: 'There is no reason why this valley should not be what it was before. But it will not happen quickly. Not in a day.'
It will be done by next harvest
questions.explain: Kumalo hopes it will happen 'before I die.'
